```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(222)
theme_set(theme_bw(18))

# Coral bleaching data from Monday (simulated)
set.seed(123)
n_per_region <- 40
coral_params <- tibble(
  region = factor(
    c("Coolest", "Moderate", "Warmest"),
    levels = c("Coolest", "Moderate", "Warmest")
  ),
  sst_mean = c(28, 29, 30),
  region_effect = c(0, -20, -40)
)
beta_0 <- -151
beta_sst <- 8
sigma <- 5

coral <- coral_params |>
  slice(rep(1:3, each = n_per_region)) |>
  mutate(
    peak_sst = rnorm(n(), sst_mean, 0.5),
    percent_bleached = beta_0 +
      beta_sst * peak_sst +
      region_effect +
      rnorm(n(), 0, sigma)
  ) |>
  select(region, peak_sst, percent_bleached)

region_lm <- lm(percent_bleached ~ region, coral)
sst_region_lm <- lm(percent_bleached ~ peak_sst + region, coral)

# Helper for the y = mx + b slides: one line per level of x2
plot_lines <- function(lines, x2_label = "x2") {
  lines |>
    mutate(x2 = factor(x2)) |>
    ggplot() +
    geom_abline(aes(intercept = b, slope = m, linetype = x2), linewidth = 1.2) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 10)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-15, 20)) +
    labs(x = "x1", y = "y", linetype = x2_label) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

# Interactions

## Today's agenda

1. Categorical predictors with >2 levels
2. Moving between representations
3. Prepare for concept mapping

# Categorical predictors with >2 levels

## Categorical predictors with 2 levels

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}

Recall the American birds experiment. _Anchor_ had two levels: 50 and 70.

$$
\text{Perc. CA} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 (\text{Anchor}=70) + \epsilon
$$

- The **reference level** (Anchor = 50) is absorbed into the intercept, $\beta_0$
- A **dummy variable** $(\text{Anchor}=70)$ is 1 for anchor 70 and 0 otherwise

::: {.fragment}

| Anchor | $(\text{Anchor}=70)$ | Mean |
|--------|:--------------------:|------|
| 50     | 0                    | $\beta_0$ |
| 70     | 1                    | $\beta_0 + \beta_1$ |

:::

:::

## Categorical predictor with 3 levels

::: {style="font-size:0.75em"}

Recall the coral bleaching data. _Region_ has **three** levels: Coolest, Moderate, Warmest.

- **Reference level**: Coolest (absorbed into $\beta_0$)
- **TWO dummy variables**: $(\text{Region}=\text{Moderate})$ and $(\text{Region}=\text{Warmest})$

::: {.fragment}

| Region   | $(\text{Moderate})$ | $(\text{Warmest})$ | Mean |
|----------|:-------------------:|:------------------:|------|
| Coolest  | 0 | 0 | $\beta_0$ |
| Moderate | 1 | 0 | $\beta_0 + \beta_1$ |
| Warmest  | 0 | 1 | $\beta_0 + \beta_2$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

A categorical predictor with $k$ levels needs $k - 1$ dummy variables.

:::

:::

## In equation form

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}
$$
\begin{align}
\text{Perc. bleached} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 (\text{Region}=\text{Moderate}) \\
&\quad + \beta_2 (\text{Region}=\text{Warmest}) + \epsilon \\
\epsilon &\sim Normal(0, \sigma)
\end{align}
$$
:::

- $\beta_0$: mean bleaching in the **Coolest** region
- $\beta_1$: difference between **Moderate** and Coolest
- $\beta_2$: difference between **Warmest** and Coolest

::: {.fragment}

What's the difference between Warmest and Moderate?

:::

::: {.fragment}

$\beta_2 - \beta_1$

:::

## In visual form

```{r}
#| fig-align: center

region_means <- tibble(region = levels(coral$region)) |>
  mutate(
    region = factor(region, levels = levels(coral$region)),
    percent_bleached = predict(region_lm, newdata = pick(everything()))
  )
ref_mean <- region_means$percent_bleached[1]

ggplot(coral, aes(region, percent_bleached)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(fill = region), shape = 21, width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ref_mean, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_segment(
    aes(xend = region, y = ref_mean, yend = percent_bleached),
    region_means[-1, ],
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")),
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_point(data = region_means, size = 5, shape = "diamond") +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0.6,
    y = ref_mean + 4,
    label = "beta[0]",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 7
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 2.25,
    y = mean(c(ref_mean, region_means$percent_bleached[2])),
    label = "beta[1]",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 7
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 3.25,
    y = mean(c(ref_mean, region_means$percent_bleached[3])),
    label = "beta[2]",
    parse = TRUE,
    size = 7
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "RdYlBu", direction = -1, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Region", y = "Percent bleached", caption = "Simulated data")
```

## In computational form

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}

```{r}
#| echo: true

region_lm <- lm(percent_bleached ~ region, coral)
summary(region_lm)
```

:::

## Continuous + categorical: equation

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}
$$
\begin{align}
\text{Perc. bleached} &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Peak SST} \\
&\quad + \beta_2 (\text{Region}=\text{Moderate}) \\
&\quad + \beta_3 (\text{Region}=\text{Warmest}) + \epsilon \\
\epsilon &\sim Normal(0, \sigma)
\end{align}
$$
:::

::: {.fragment}

| Region   | Intercept | Slope |
|----------|-----------|-------|
| Coolest  | $\beta_0$ | $\beta_1$ |
| Moderate | $\beta_0 + \beta_2$ | $\beta_1$ |
| Warmest  | $\beta_0 + \beta_3$ | $\beta_1$ |

:::

::: {.fragment}

Three parallel lines: same slope, different intercepts.

:::

## Continuous + categorical: visual

```{r}
#| fig-align: center

coral |>
  mutate(fit = predict(sst_region_lm)) |>
  ggplot(aes(peak_sst, percent_bleached, fill = region)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, color = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = fit, color = region), linewidth = 1.5) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "RdYlBu", direction = -1) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "RdYlBu", direction = -1) +
  labs(
    x = "Peak SST (degC)",
    y = "Percent bleached",
    fill = "Region",
    color = "Region",
    caption = "Simulated data"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}

```{r}
#| echo: true

sst_region_lm <- lm(percent_bleached ~ peak_sst + region, coral)
summary(sst_region_lm)
```

# Moving between representations

## Review of $y = mx + b$

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1
$$

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}

What are $m$ and $b$?

::: {.fragment}

- $m = \beta_1$
- $b = \beta_0$

:::

:::

::: {.column width="60%" .fragment}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5

plot_lines(tibble(x2 = "-", b = 2, m = 1.5)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

:::

:::

## Categorical $x_2$, additive

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2
$$

$x_2$ is **categorical** (A or B). What are $m$ and $b$ for each level?

::: {.columns style="font-size:0.75em"}

::: {.column .fragment}

**A** ($x_2 = 0$)

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (0) \\
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1
\end{align}
$$

$m = \beta_1$, $b = \beta_0$

:::

::: {.column .fragment}

**B** ($x_2 = 1$)

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (1) \\
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 \\
y &= \left( \beta_0 + \beta_2 \right) + \beta_1 x_1
\end{align}
$$

$m = \beta_1$, $b = \beta_0 + \beta_2$

:::

:::

## Categorical $x_2$, additive: summary

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2
$$

::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

| $x_2$ | $m$ | $b$ |
|-------|-----|-----|
| A (0) | $\beta_1$ | $\beta_0$ |
| B (1) | $\beta_1$ | $\beta_0 + \beta_2$ |

Same slope, different intercepts.

:::

::: {.column}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5

plot_lines(tibble(x2 = c("A", "B"), b = c(2, 2 - 4), m = 1.5))
```

:::

:::

## Continuous $x_2$, additive

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2
$$

$x_2$ is **continuous**. What are $m$ and $b$ when $x_2$ is 0, 1, or 2?

::: {.columns style="font-size:0.65em"}

::: {.column width="33%" .fragment}

$x_2 = 0$

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (0) \\
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1
\end{align}
$$

$m = \beta_1$, $b = \beta_0$

:::

::: {.column width="33%" .fragment}

$x_2 = 1$

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (1) \\
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 \\
y &= \left( \beta_0 + \beta_2 \right) + \beta_1 x_1
\end{align}
$$

$m = \beta_1$, $b = \beta_0 + \beta_2$

:::

::: {.column width="33%" .fragment}

$x_2 = 2$

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (2) \\
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + 2 \beta_2 \\
y &= \left( \beta_0 + 2 \beta_2 \right) + \beta_1 x_1
\end{align}
$$

$m = \beta_1$, $b = \beta_0 + 2 \beta_2$

:::

:::

## Continuous $x_2$, additive: summary

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2
$$

::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

| $x_2$ | $m$ | $b$ |
|-------|-----|-----|
| 0 | $\beta_1$ | $\beta_0$ |
| 1 | $\beta_1$ | $\beta_0 + \beta_2$ |
| 2 | $\beta_1$ | $\beta_0 + 2\beta_2$ |

Same slope, intercept shifts by $\beta_2$ per unit of $x_2$.

:::

::: {.column}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5

plot_lines(tibble(x2 = 0:2, b = 2 - 4 * x2, m = 1.5))
```

:::

:::

## Categorical $x_2$, interactive

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 + \beta_3 x_1 x_2
$$

$x_2$ is **categorical** (A or B). What are $m$ and $b$ for each level?

::: {.columns style="font-size:0.75em"}

::: {.column .fragment}

**A** ($x_2 = 0$)

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (0) + \beta_3 x_1 (0) \\
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1
\end{align}
$$

$m = \beta_1$, $b = \beta_0$

:::

::: {.column .fragment}

**B** ($x_2 = 1$)

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (1) + \beta_3 x_1 (1) \\
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 + \beta_3 x_1 \\
y &= \left( \beta_0 + \beta_2 \right) + \left( \beta_1 + \beta_3 \right) x_1
\end{align}
$$

$m = \beta_1 + \beta_3$, $b = \beta_0 + \beta_2$

:::

:::

## Categorical $x_2$, interactive: summary

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 + \beta_3 x_1 x_2
$$

::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

| $x_2$ | $m$ | $b$ |
|-------|-----|-----|
| A (0) | $\beta_1$ | $\beta_0$ |
| B (1) | $\beta_1 + \beta_3$ | $\beta_0 + \beta_2$ |

Different slopes **and** different intercepts.

:::

::: {.column}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5

plot_lines(tibble(x2 = c("A", "B"), b = c(2, 2 - 4), m = c(1.5, 1.5 - 2)))
```

:::

:::

## Continuous $x_2$, interactive

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 + \beta_3 x_1 x_2
$$

$x_2$ is **continuous**. What are $m$ and $b$ when $x_2$ is 0, 1, or 2?

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.65em"}

$x_2 = 0$: $\quad y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (0) + \beta_3 x_1 (0) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 \quad$ so $m = \beta_1$, $b = \beta_0$

:::

::: {.columns style="font-size:0.65em"}

::: {.column .fragment}

$x_2 = 1$

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (1) + \beta_3 x_1 (1) \\
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 + \beta_3 x_1 \\
y &= \left( \beta_0 + \beta_2 \right) + \left( \beta_1 + \beta_3 \right) x_1
\end{align}
$$

$m = \beta_1 + \beta_3$, $b = \beta_0 + \beta_2$

:::

::: {.column .fragment}

$x_2 = 2$

$$
\begin{align}
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 (2) + \beta_3 x_1 (2) \\
y &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + 2 \beta_2 + 2 \beta_3 x_1 \\
y &= \left( \beta_0 + 2 \beta_2 \right) + \left( \beta_1 + 2 \beta_3 \right) x_1
\end{align}
$$

$m = \beta_1 + 2 \beta_3$, $b = \beta_0 + 2 \beta_2$

:::

:::

## Continuous $x_2$, interactive: summary

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 + \beta_3 x_1 x_2
$$

::: {.columns}

::: {.column}

| $x_2$ | $m$ | $b$ |
|-------|-----|-----|
| 0 | $\beta_1$ | $\beta_0$ |
| 1 | $\beta_1 + \beta_3$ | $\beta_0 + \beta_2$ |
| 2 | $\beta_1 + 2\beta_3$ | $\beta_0 + 2\beta_2$ |

Slope shifts by $\beta_3$ and intercept by $\beta_2$ per unit of $x_2$.

:::

::: {.column}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5

plot_lines(tibble(x2 = 0:2, b = 2 - 4 * x2, m = 1.5 - 1 * x2))
```

:::

:::

## Moving between representations worksheet

Every model can be written three ways. Practice translating between them.

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"themeVariables": {"fontSize": "24px"}}}%%
flowchart LR
    eq["<b>Equation</b><br/>y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₁x₂"]
    vis["<b>Visual</b><br/>lines, slopes, intercepts"]
    comp["<b>Computational</b><br/>lm() and summary()"]
    eq <--> vis
    vis <--> comp
    comp <--> eq
```

Given one representation, produce the other two.
